title: Distribution dynamics of climatically suitable areas over the 21st century of two direct-development anurans (Anura: Brachycephalidae) in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
content:
Abstract
Climate change especially affects species distributions that depend on specific environmental variables related to reproduction, such as direct-development anurans from the Brachycephalidae family. Owing to the dynamic and multiple climate change scenarios expected for the next decades, we aimed to provide range predictions for four successive time slices over the 21st century (2030, 2050, 2070, and 2090) and under three greenhouse gas emission scenarios for Ischnocnema henselii and Ischnocnema parva. By performing ecological niche modelling procedures, we found that climate change is presumed to reduce predictive areas of I. henselii at magnitudes varying from ∼48% to 96% of the present-day prediction by the end of the 21st century, depending on the CO2 emission scenario. For I. parva, our predictions point out that a much smaller area is expected to be lost by 2050 (<34% of the present-day predicted area), with an associated recovery of predictive areas expected after 2070 for some CO2 emission scenarios. By the end of the 21st century, both species are predicted to become restricted to coastal populations, thus posing serious concerns to their northern and inland populations, whose areas are likely to become climatically unsuitable under climate change scenarios.
